elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section 9.1 caps IBM ("IBM is liable for no more than") and the parallel Section 9.2 caps Customer ("Customer is liable for no more than"), each at the same greater-of formula, so the cap runs both ways.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Retained text reads "up to the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim": the floor is $100,000 not USD 1,000,000, the basis is charges "paid" only (not paid or payable), and the anchor is accrual of the first claim rather than the claim in question.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section 10.a: "In no event will either party be liable to the other for special, incidental, or indirect damages or for any consequential damages (including lost profits or savings)" — expressly bilateral (the carve-back only preserves Customer's payment obligations).

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The limitations and exclusions of liability in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 do not apply to a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations..." The retained Section 6 priority sentence (Sections 5, 9 and 10 prevail over inconsistent confidentiality-agreement terms) does not contradict it, because the new carve-out is itself part of Section 9.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The inserted carve-out names only confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out appears, and Section 9.1(c) still disclaims liability for loss of or damage to Customer records or data. Drafter must add "its data protection and security obligations" to the carve-out sentence.

Indemnification sits as a separate limb outside the monetary cap in limb (c): 9.1(a) "indemnification payments as provided in Section 8.1" and 9.2(a) "Indemnification payments as provided in Section 8.2"; only "any other actual direct damages" are subject to the greater-of figure.
Inserted sentence disapplies Sections 9.1 and 9.2 to "its gross negligence", mutually ("a party's").
Inserted sentence disapplies Sections 9.1 and 9.2 to "its willful misconduct" for either party.
No fraud carve-out anywhere in Sections 9, 10 or the inserted sentence; add "fraud" to the carve-out list.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Neither the retained caps nor the inserted sentence carve out IP infringement; the Section 8 indemnities are a different animal (third-party claims), so a party's direct infringement of the other's IP remains inside the $100,000/12-month cap.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Only Section 10 (consequential damages) carves back Customer's failure to pay; Section 9.2's cap on "any other actual direct damages" still captures Customer's payment obligations. An express statement that Customer's obligation to pay charges is not "damages" subject to Section 9.2 is required.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Parallel caps in Sections 9.1 (IBM) and 9.2 (Customer) on identical terms; no unlimited-Customer-liability language remains.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "up to the greater of $100,000 or the charges paid by Customer to IBM for the Services in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the accrual of the first claim related to the Services" — a twelve-month charges basis with a floor, comfortably above the 6-month walk-away line.
9.1(a)/9.2(a) list indemnification payments as a distinct limb; the greater-of figure applies only to limb (c) "any other actual direct damages".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: New sentence: limitations and exclusions in 9.1 and 9.2 "do not apply to a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations".
New sentence expressly disapplies the 9.1/9.2 limits to "its gross negligence" for both parties.
New sentence expressly disapplies the 9.1/9.2 limits to "its willful misconduct" for both parties.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: mutual caps (9.1/9.2), a twelve-month charges basis with a $100,000 floor, indemnification already outside the capped limb, and the single inserted sentence supplying the three missing carve-outs (confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct) on a mutual basis.

Preferred level fails on five elements: the floor is $100,000 rather than USD 1,000,000 and the basis is charges "paid" measured from accrual of the first claim (not "paid or payable" in the 12 months preceding the claim); no data protection/security carve-out; no fraud carve-out; no carve-out for infringement of the other party's IP; and Customer's payment obligations are not excluded from damages subject to Section 9.2 (the Section 10 proviso only addresses consequential damages).

Minimal: one inserted sentence, no deletions, no survival tails, expense language, procedures or extra damages categories, and it carves out exactly the three fallback items that were missing; the existing favourable Section 10 mutual consequential-damages exclusion and the Section 9.2 third-party-claim protection are left intact.

Intent preserved: the inserted sentence cross-refers to existing Sections 9.1 and 9.2, leaves no undefined term or dangling reference, and does not contradict the retained Section 6 priority sentence, since the carve-out forms part of Section 9 which that sentence gives precedence.

If the counterparty accepts the carve-out sentence, the drafter should next pursue the preferred-level items by amending limb (c) to "the greater of USD 1,000,000 or the fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim", extending the carve-out list to data protection/security, fraud and infringement of the other party's IP, and adding that Customer's obligation to pay charges is not "damages" for purposes of Section 9.2.
